behavioral_notes.observation: Inbound emails to a job's mail alias auto-create hr.applicant records (alias_model = hr.applicant) with alias_defaults seeding job_id/department_id/company_id/user_id and the job's first stage; hr.job.platform regex parses the applicant's name out of job-board emails (e.g. LinkedIn) so CVs/applications can be ingested by email. Not visible in metadata.

Hire conversion: creates an hr.employee from the applicant via _get_employee_create_vals (name, work_contact_id, job_id, job_title, department_id, private address), copies the applicant's unique ir.attachment files (CV/docs) onto the new employee, and back-links applicant_ids. This is the recruitment->HR core handoff, driven by Python not schema.

stage_id drives the kanban pipeline (stage.fold + legend_blocked/waiting/done/normal + applicant.kanban_state). Moving into a stage flagged hired_stage sets date_closed (via _compute_date_closed) and decrements hr.job.no_of_recruitment (openings); leaving it increments it back. Stages with a template_id post an automated email to the applicant on entry (_track_template). _read_group_stage_ids/group_expand keep empty columns visible.

Interview scheduling opens the calendar action and creates calendar.event records linked back through calendar.event.applicant_id, defaulting attendees to the applicant + recruiter/department manager. Setting interviewer_ids calls _create_recruitment_interviewers (granting interviewer-group access) and message_notify's the assigned interviewers. Cross-model side-effect into calendar, invisible in metadata.

_get_similar_applicants_domain / _search_is_applicant_in_pool match applicants across email_normalized, partner_phone_sanitized and linkedin_profile (the pool search uses a raw SQL CTE), powering application_count, talent_pool_count and de-duplication when adding talents to a pool. Behavior lives in compute/search methods, not field metadata.

value_streams: Source-to-Hire: job opening -> application intake -> screening/stages -> interviews -> offer -> hired employee
policies: 8 record rules: interviewer-only visibility (see only applicants on their jobs), multi-company scoping, recruiter ownership

classification.rationale: hr_recruitment is a talent-acquisition support activity: it does not produce or sell the firm's output but supplies the organization with human capital. It maps to APQC PCF 7.1 (Recruit, source and select employees) and feeds hr (hr.employee) at the hire boundary. As an HR support function it is a 'support' value model (infrastructure/staffing) rather than a primary value-chain activity; no document flow to stock/account, the terminal output is a hired hr.employee.

standard_capabilities: job-position management with per-job email alias intake
applicant pipeline with configurable kanban stages (fold, hired_stage, rotting threshold)
interview scheduling through calendar + interviewer assignment/notification
talent pool with email/phone/LinkedIn duplicate detection
UTM sourcing (medium/source/campaign) and job-platform regex parsing
one-click hire: create employee from applicant (CV/attachments copied)
typical_fits: standard source-to-hire pipeline driven by kanban stages
interviewer access scoping via record rules
common_gaps: online job board / careers website (separate module website_hr_recruitment)
custom approval workflow for offers / salary bands

open_questions: Default recruitment stages shipped as data are New, Qualification, First Interview, Second Interview, Contract Proposal, Contract Signed; which are job-specific vs global at runtime is config-dependent.
